source: Majles Al Ihsa consultation 2026-05-03 — Miriam Oduya-Schwarzkopf (#19, Stats 3 / Empirical Bayes / hierarchical priors)
purpose: indicator-to-sector mapping for Empirical Bayes hyperprior estimation. The (sector x L1) cells determine which indicators share a Beta(alpha(s,L1), beta(s,L1)) prior. Wrong cells -> wrong pooling -> wrong shrinkage.

cohort_counts.cohort_glossary: n_indicators_in_taxonomy: planned/curated catalog scope at the time of generation (this file). Includes future not-yet-ingested indicators. n_indicators_currently_ingested: indicators with rows in qgi_data.scdis (source-of-truth: indicator-stationarity-audit-v2.json, 109 results as of 2026-05-11). n_indicators_with_direction_annotations: indicators with a curated direction (+1/0/-1) for signed-scoring in Phase 5 (source-of-truth: indicator-directions.json, 104 entries as of 2026-05-11). These three cohorts are NOT stale snapshots of the same number; they are three different populations. Coverage delta from build_indicator_directions.py: audited=109 in_directions=104 covered=87 audited_but_missing=22 in_directions_but_not_audited=17. Reconciliation work tracked at #653.

CONFLICT.name: Armed Conflict & Violence
CONFLICT.definition: Indicators whose primary signal is the incidence, intensity, or direct human cost of organized armed violence (state and non-state).

DISPLACE.name: Displacement & Migration
DISPLACE.definition: Indicators measuring forced or voluntary population movement across or within borders as the primary measured phenomenon.

GOV_INST.name: Governance & Institutional Quality
GOV_INST.definition: Indicators measuring how effectively formal political and legal institutions function — democracy indices, rule of law, judicial independence, electoral process, legislative constraints.

REPRESSION.name: State Repression & Civil Liberties
REPRESSION.definition: Indicators measuring the degree to which the state suppresses physical, political, or expressive freedom of its population — torture, killings, censorship, repression of civil society.

ECON_FISC.name: Economic & Fiscal Stress
ECON_FISC.definition: Indicators measuring government balance-sheet fragility, sovereign debt, banking system health, and macro-economic vulnerability to crisis.

LABOR_SOC.name: Labor Market & Social Conditions
LABOR_SOC.definition: Indicators measuring employment quality, wage dynamics, inequality, poverty, and the social infrastructure that determines population resilience to economic shocks.

FOOD_RES.name: Food Security & Natural Resources
FOOD_RES.definition: Indicators measuring agricultural output, food availability, dietary security, land use, water stress, and environmental resource base.

DIPLO_GEO.name: Diplomatic & Geopolitical Signal
DIPLO_GEO.definition: Indicators capturing how countries relate to each other through events, media coverage, and the internationalization of conflict — primarily GDELT-derived news-event aggregates plus sovereignty indicators.

SOC_MOBIL.name: Social Mobilization & Identity
SOC_MOBIL.definition: Indicators measuring organized citizen action, political participation, power distribution across social groups, and gender/ethnic inclusion — the substrate for mass protest and social reform events.

STRUCT_DEV.name: Structural Development Context
STRUCT_DEV.definition: Indicators measuring long-run human capital, education, and basic development trajectories that serve as slow-moving structural moderators rather than active event precursors.

known_weaknesses: DIPLO_GEO contains 21 indicators with substantial within-sector correlation (multiple GDELT facets of the same media-coverage process). Likely violates Beta exchangeability. Phase 4 surfaces this as high posterior variance; fix is to split into DIPLO_MEDIA + DIPLO_STRUCT.

STRUCT_DEV has only 4 indicators — below comfortable EB floor. Defensible because the 4 share a genuinely distinct (near-flat) frequency profile that would corrupt other sectors if pooled. Phase 4 test: compare STRUCT_DEV EB prior to flat Beta(1,1) — if no measurable shrinkage improvement, dissolve and reassign WB-06/WB-07 to GOV_INST and UD-05/UD-06 to LABOR_SOC.

WB-06.rationale: Business startup cost moderates at structural/institutional speed, not crisis speed; does not spike in banking crises.

WB-07.rationale: Contract enforcement time is essentially flat; almost never spikes with crises. Structural moderator, not active precursor.

WB-08.rationale: Diaspora-economy linkage; tracks labor market in destination countries. Not DISPLACE (no conflict driver) nor ECON_FISC (no sovereign balance-sheet signal).

WB-09.rationale: Banking_crisis link decisive — co-varies with NPLs and bank assets more than with youth unemployment. Borderline with LABOR_SOC.

WB-15.rationale: ODA donor generosity is a fiscal-policy output. Borderline with DIPLO_GEO; if recipient-side coverage expands, reassign.

WB-P1.rationale: Remittances received — household income at population scale (recipient side of WB-08).

WB-P6.rationale: Women in parliament framed as institutional quality proxy; co-varies with VD-01/VD-32 more than with VD-26 across event categories. Borderline with SOC_MOBIL.

VD-06.rationale: Polarization is a political-process indicator (institutional dysfunction), not rights-violation or mobilization.

VD-11.rationale: State capacity (institutional) vs balance-sheet stress (fiscal). Co-varies with VD-03/VD-04 not WB-10. GOV_INST.

VD-16.rationale: Property-rights/freedom-of-movement collapse → migration. State withdrawal of rights, not citizen-organized action.

VD-21.rationale: Legitimacy collapse triggers protest/coup; co-varies with VD-09/VD-28 (mobilization triggers). Borderline with GOV_INST.

VD-30.rationale: Strongest structural predictor of civil war onset (Cederman/Wimmer), but moves on decade timescales. SOC_MOBIL prior captures slow structural conditions; CONFLICT prior would over-shrink toward crisis-frequency.

FA-03.rationale: Food price volatility — supply-chain phenomenon, not sovereign balance-sheet. Co-varies with FA-01/FA-14, not WB-13.

UN-05.rationale: Voluntary returns mirror UN-01/UN-03 with lag — same country-level conditions drive both.

UN-06.rationale: Stateless persons — chronic sub-stock of displacement, not active repression event. Borderline with REPRESSION.

ID-01.rationale: Measurement object is conflict activity, not population management.

ID-02.rationale: Disaster displacement tracks climate exposure + agricultural fragility (FOOD_RES vulnerabilities), not conflict.

ID-03.rationale: Chronic conflict-origin stock; signal is unresolved conflict, not population management.

UD-05.rationale: Mean years of schooling — slow-moving human capital stock; does not spike with crises.

UD-06.rationale: Same rationale as UD-05; forward-looking human capital.

OW-04.rationale: CO2 growth as economic activity proxy (resource boom / deindustrialization), not environmental governance.

GD-07.rationale: GDELT protest counts are media-coverage artifacts (50× source duplication), not ground-truth mobilization. Co-varies with GD-04/GD-15, not VD-25/VD-28.

GD-14.rationale: Material conflict events are the 'hard signal' GDELT indicator — actual fighting. Co-varies with WB-01/UC-01 more than with GD-02 diplomatic score.
